name: Dead Cluster Flow — Dead Cluster → Snatch → Iron Cross → Outside Pendulum → Tactical Clean → Reverse Lunge → Offset Rack Squat
description: A full-body single-bell kettlebell flow from a Madeleine Conti reel (her '2nd most saved & shared kettlebell flow of 2025') — the ballistic, overhead cousin to the Leggy Flow (kb-leggy-flow). Where the Leggy Flow stays at the rack and works the legs laterally, this one goes overhead: a dead cluster from the floor, a snatch, an iron-cross lateral hold, an outside pendulum swing, then a tactical clean into a reverse lunge and an offset rack squat. Run the whole sequence on one side, then the other. Overhead-heavy — go LIGHT and mind the right shoulder on the snatch, cluster press, and iron cross.
flowNotes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side — dead cluster → snatch → iron cross → outside pendulum → inside tactical clean → reverse lunge → offset rack squat — letting each move feed the next, then repeat on the other side. Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell; quality and continuity over load. Unlike the Leggy Flow, this one is **overhead-heavy** (dead cluster press, snatch, iron cross) — keep the load conservative and mind the right shoulder: pack the shoulder down on every overhead beat, and regress or skip the iron cross if it flares. The cleans, snatch, and pendulum come from the legs and hips, not the arm. 3 rounds each side.

flowSequence.notes: Dead clean off the floor → front squat → drive up into a press to overhead, then lower to the rack and set the bell down dead for the next rep. Legs clean it, legs squat it, legs drive the press — no grinding the press from the shoulder.

In this flow the snatch lives overhead-to-overhead, not floor-to-overhead like a standalone snatch. Carry straight from the dead cluster's overhead lockout — don't reset to the floor: lower the bell out of the lockout and snatch it right back up overhead in one arc, hips driving it, punch the hand through to a soft catch on the forearm.

Straight-arm raise the bell out to the side to shoulder height — a 'T' / crucifix hold. Shoulder packed DOWN (not shrugged), arm parallel to the floor, brief hold. Big straight-arm shoulder load — go light, back off if the right shoulder complains.

Two full single-arm pendulum swings out around the working hip, driven by the legs — brace the core so the torso doesn't twist toward the bell. Let it float at the top and pendulum back; the second swing's inside arc feeds straight into the tactical clean that follows, so don't stop dead between them.
Coming directly out of the second pendulum swing — thread the bell on the 'inside' path into the rack, no reset, no momentum yank, no forearm bang. Sets up the lunge and squat that follow.
Bell stays racked. Step the trailing leg straight back, both knees to ~90°, torso tall, drive through the front heel to stand. The offset rack load makes the core fight the pull to the loaded side.
Bell racked on the one side, squat — chest tall, racked elbow up, resist the pull toward the loaded side, full depth, drive up through the whole foot. Closes the flow before switching sides.

tips: This is a FLOW — the seven moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Smooth, controlled transitions are the point.
Single LIGHT-to-MEDIUM bell — movement quality and continuity over load. The cleans, snatch, and pendulum are powered by the legs and hips, not the arm.
Run the full sequence on one side, then the other. 3 rounds each side is a solid dose; for a conditioning version, run 2-3 rounds/side as one set, rest 1 min, repeat for 4-5 sets.

**Overhead-heavy, unlike the Leggy Flow** — the dead cluster press, snatch, and iron cross all load the shoulder overhead / on a long lever. Pack the shoulder DOWN on every overhead beat, keep the load conservative, and regress or skip the iron cross if the right shoulder flares.
Great for full-body power, overhead stability, grip, lateral-plane conditioning, and coordination.
